loc.ooku.title: The Ōoku of Edo Castle
loc.ooku.body: The innermost palace of Edo Castle, where no man but the shogun may enter. All three films take place here, in long corridors hung with lanterns and purple curtains.

loc.wanya.title: The Yorozuya on a rainy night
loc.wanya.body: An old inn in the rain, once a brothel. On the top floor is a large room never given to guests. The first story of the TV series begins here.

wanya_genkan.1.title: The stained-glass door
wanya_genkan.1.body: Just inside is a stained-glass door, Western glass set into a wooden Japanese inn. That rainy night a woman pushed it open and asked for a room. Only the one on the top floor was left.

wanya_rouka.1.title: The octagonal hall upstairs
wanya_rouka.1.body: Several corridors meet here. Half-moons of stained glass sit above the doorways, and blue Western chairs stand on the floor. The guests have all gone to bed, yet there are footsteps on the boards. Who is running?

wanya_rouka.2.title: The pointed katōmado
wanya_rouka.2.body: This pointed, latticed window is called a katōmado, once used mostly in temples. The deeper the corridor goes, the quieter it gets, until only the rain outside is left.

wanya_ozashiki.1.title: The room kept from guests
wanya_ozashiki.1.body: The largest zashiki on the top floor, a gold screen behind its raised dais. It is never given to guests. That rainy night, a guest with child moved in. What happened in this room before?

ooku_corridor.1.title: The red-and-white fan doorway
ooku_corridor.1.body: The main corridor ends at a doorway painted with red and white fans. The ladies-in-waiting pass here all day, and not one step may break the rules. An old paper umbrella is tucked by the wall. Who left it here?

ooku_corridor.2.title: The great mural
ooku_corridor.2.body: The whole wall is painted with ukiyo-e beauties, their faces many times life size. The films' Ōoku is thick with colour, wall over curtain over lantern. Everyone in the painting is smiling.

ooku_maids.1.title: The round window
ooku_maids.1.body: The ladies-in-waiting sleep here. Peonies and butterflies cover the fusuma on all four sides, with a round window in the middle. New arrivals live here. Where did the things they brought from home go?

ooku_utayama.1.title: Crane screen and writing desk
ooku_utayama.1.body: Finer than the maids' quarters: a screen of pines and cranes, a low writing desk before it. In the Ōoku, the higher the rank, the quieter the room. Does the one who makes the rules have something she couldn't throw away?

ooku_yuki.1.title: The empty room
ooku_yuki.1.body: Peeling walls, worn tatami, a closet door shut tight. The Ōoku is full of people, yet this one room stands empty. Oyuki lived here once. Where did she go?

ooku_courtyard.1.title: The courtyard well
ooku_courtyard.1.body: A new lady-in-waiting must drop her most treasured possession into this well, to cut herself off from life outside. So many things thrown down. What does the bottom look like now?

wanya_soto.1.title: Arriving at the Yorozuya
wanya_soto.1.body: The rain hasn't let up. A canal runs past the front; over the red arched bridge is the main gate, under a curving karahafu roof. Every lantern upstairs is lit except on the top floor. Who is staying there?

wanya_soto.2.title: Shadows by the bridge
wanya_soto.2.body: A few ink-black figures stand by the red bridge, their faces unclear. They don't come in. They only look up at the floors above.

wanya_niwa.1.title: A garden indoors
wanya_niwa.1.body: Step in from the octagonal hall and there is a garden inside the house: white sand, a stream down the middle, a red arched bridge. The rain is outside. In here it is so quiet it hardly feels like part of the building.

wanya_niwa.2.title: Stones on white sand
wanya_niwa.2.body: Four garden stones of different sizes sit on the white sand. Behind them, a few small figures peek out. Who are they here for?

wanya_soto.3.title: The Yorozuya from the street
wanya_soto.3.body: From the street corner the building rises tier on tier, a karahafu gable and a round sign at its centre, stone lanterns on either side. Too grand a front for an ordinary inn. What was this place before?

loc.sakai.title: The Sakai samurai house
loc.sakai.body: A samurai household on the day its daughter marries. Everyone is busy with the wedding, yet there isn't a single cat in the house. The Medicine Seller's first appearance, and the story the Bakeneko name comes from.

sakai_omote.1.title: The gate dressed for a wedding
sakai_omote.1.body: The tiled gatehouse is hung with a great red curtain bearing the white family crest, crest lanterns on either side. It's lively out front. A house this big, and not one cat to be heard.

sakai_genkan.1.title: The doma at the entrance
sakai_genkan.1.body: Inside is a stone-paved doma, and only one step up are you really in the house. The guests have been shown to the reception room. The old master sits at the head and says nothing.

sakai_rouka.1.title: The red corridor
sakai_rouka.1.body: A long corridor lacquered red runs deep into the house. The farther you walk, the longer it gets. There is a door at the end, and the servants go around it when they carry things.

sakai_kyakuma.1.title: Round cushions
sakai_kyakuma.1.body: The room for receiving guests. A rooster on the fusuma, pines and cranes on the screen, cushions in red and blue. The old master keeps looking at the crane. He looks for a long time.

sakai_ozashiki.1.title: The wedding zashiki
sakai_ozashiki.1.body: The great zashiki for the wedding: curling waves on the fusuma, a carpet patterned with cranes, a gold screen at the far end. The guests have left their places.

sakai_misshitsu.1.title: The room with the shiromuku
sakai_misshitsu.1.body: A room deep in the house that no one may enter, green walls and red lattice, a white shiromuku laid out at the front. A family holding a wedding, and the bridal robe is kept this far in?

sakai_daidokoro.1.title: A kitchen with no cat
sakai_daidokoro.1.body: A doma with a stove, a wooden worktable and a row of clay jars, several mousetraps on the floor. Mice, traps, and not one cat. Do they not keep one, or not dare to?

sakai_daidokoro.2.title: The old well out back
sakai_daidokoro.2.body: Behind the house is an old well in a wooden frame, a small grave before it. The flowers are fresh. The front is so busy, yet someone keeps remembering to come here. Who is buried in it?

mononoke.sakai.name: Bakeneko
mononoke.sakai.katachi: In a house with no cats, a Bakeneko appeared.
mononoke.sakai.makoto: Years ago, a woman was shut away deep in this house.
mononoke.sakai.kotowari: She died there, and her cat remembered this family.
mononoke.sakai.itemBody: A small bell on an old red cord, its clapper long rusted still. Its owner used to hear it ring every day.
mononoke.sakai.after: The bell fades away. It no longer has to guard this house.

mononoke.wanya.name: Zashiki-warashi
mononoke.wanya.katachi: Running all through the rooms: Zashiki-warashi.
mononoke.wanya.makoto: In the years this was a brothel, there were children who were never born.
mononoke.wanya.kotowari: They only wanted to be born, to have a mother who would keep them.
mononoke.wanya.itemBody: The thread has loosened and the colour gone dull. With no one to play with, it has kept rolling about that top-floor room.
mononoke.wanya.after: The children stop knocking. They go to find someone who will keep them.

mononoke.ooku.name: Karakasa
mononoke.ooku.katachi: Opening by itself in the rain: a Karakasa.
mononoke.ooku.makoto: Everyone who enters the Ōoku throws part of herself into the well.
mononoke.ooku.kotowari: What was thrown away won't simply sink.
mononoke.ooku.itemBody: Two ribs broken, the paper waterlogged. Old things that are thrown away sometimes open up on their own.
mononoke.ooku.after: What was thrown in the well finally lets go.

mononoke.noppera.name: Noppera-bō
mononoke.noppera.katachi: She turned around, and there was nothing on her face.
mononoke.noppera.makoto: In this house she had to put on a new face for the guests every day.
mononoke.noppera.kotowari: After so long, she couldn't find her own face again.
mononoke.noppera.itemBody: A mask painted white, with no eyes or brows drawn. Wear it, and anyone can be her.
mononoke.noppera.after: She no longer has to change faces. She left with her own.

mononoke.hinezumi.name: Hinezumi
mononoke.hinezumi.katachi: Darting under the lanterns: a Hinezumi.
mononoke.hinezumi.makoto: Someone gave her a fire-rat pelt and said it was like his heart. It would never burn.
mononoke.hinezumi.kotowari: It scorched the moment it touched flame, and she never again believed in a true heart.
mononoke.hinezumi.itemBody: They say a fire rat's pelt won't burn even in flames. This one is scorched down one side.
mononoke.hinezumi.after: The fire goes out. What was left of that feeling is let go.

mononoke.umibozu.name: Umibōzu
mononoke.umibozu.katachi: The rain fell so hard an Umibōzu rose from the water out front.
mononoke.umibozu.makoto: A boat overturned one rainy night, and no one on shore went to help.
mononoke.umibozu.kotowari: Those who sank kept waiting for someone on shore to look back.
mononoke.umibozu.itemBody: The cord has rotted through, and half the beads are gone. The night the boat went over, someone held them and prayed to the end.
mononoke.umibozu.after: The water recedes. He no longer has to wait for the shore to look back.

mononoke.nue.name: Nue
mononoke.nue.katachi: The cry on the roof at night is a Nue.
mononoke.nue.makoto: This family never said things plainly. They swallowed them into the night.
mononoke.nue.kotowari: The swallowed words ran together into something no one could name.
mononoke.nue.itemBody: A black feather from a bird no one can name. No one can say what that cry in the night was, either.
mononoke.nue.after: The words left unsaid finally have somewhere to go.

mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.name: White Bakeneko
mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.katachi: Peering out from behind the door: a White Bakeneko.
mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.makoto: This family once kept a white cat. Later it was given away.
mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.kotowari: It only wanted to come home, to the corner where it used to sleep.
mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.itemBody: A collar sewn from white cloth, a name written inside. The ink has faded.
mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.after: It is back in its old corner, sleeping soundly.

mononoke.bakeneko_ko.name: Little Bakeneko
mononoke.bakeneko_ko.katachi: Three shoot out at once, all Little Bakeneko.
mononoke.bakeneko_ko.makoto: Under the house were three kittens. Their mother never came back.
mononoke.bakeneko_ko.kotowari: They kept waiting for someone to come and feed them.
mononoke.bakeneko_ko.itemBody: Three bells the same size, strung on one thread. The bells stayed behind. The kittens' mother came for them.
mononoke.bakeneko_ko.after: Their mother came back, and the three kittens followed her away.

mononoke.karakasa_kuro.name: Black Karakasa
mononoke.karakasa_kuro.katachi: Opening dark and heavy by the well: another Karakasa.
mononoke.karakasa_kuro.makoto: The rule of the well was set by someone long ago.
mononoke.karakasa_kuro.kotowari: Even the one who made the rule had something she couldn't throw away.
mononoke.karakasa_kuro.itemBody: A few jet-black ribs, the paper long gone. It has lain at the bottom of the well longer than anything.
mononoke.karakasa_kuro.after: The one who made the rule has let hers go too.

mononoke.zashiki_ao.name: Blue Zashiki
mononoke.zashiki_ao.katachi: Following behind without a sound: a Blue Zashiki.
mononoke.zashiki_ao.makoto: A child was born in this house and grew up hidden on the top floor.
mononoke.zashiki_ao.kotowari: The child didn't want to leave. He only wanted someone to come and play.
mononoke.zashiki_ao.itemBody: A temari wound in blue thread, newer than the red one. Its owner could never bear to take it out and play.
mononoke.zashiki_ao.after: Someone finally came looking, and the child went out to play.

lines: I'm on watch tonight. A wedding's a wedding, but I'm uneasy.
At night this corridor feels like it never ends.
That door at the back. The master said no one is to open it.
There's a wedding in the house, so even an old man like me comes out to sit.
Years ago, a girl lived deep in the house. She kept a cat.
Later the cat went missing. No one went looking for it.
The kitchen's been busy since before dawn. I haven't stopped once.
No cats in this house. The master's orders.
However bad the mice get, all we can do is set traps.

hint.sakai.形: Something seems to be missing in the kitchen.
hint.sakai.真: Deepest in the house, there's a door no one has opened.
hint.sakai.理: The grave by the well. The old master remembers.

find.sakai.1.title: Scattered sweet wrappers
find.sakai.1.body: Red and white sweet wrappers, strewn on the flagstones by the gate and trodden on many times. So many have come to offer congratulations, and no one bends to pick them up.

find.sakai.2.title: Low scratches on a pillar
find.sakai.2.body: A faint scratch at the foot of a red pillar, less than a foot off the ground. The lacquer was redone once, but the mark still shows through.

find.sakai.3.title: A small upturned bowl
find.sakai.3.body: A small clay bowl lies upside down in the corner, shallow, a chip out of the rim. Turn it over and it's clean inside. No one has filled it in years.

case.sakai.title: A wedding at the Sakai house
case.sakai.hook: Halfway through the wedding, a mononoke appears in the house. Without Form, Truth and Reason, the sword stays sheathed.

note.sakai.daidokoro/view:1: The kitchen has mice and traps, but no cat.
note.sakai.daidokoro/npc:kayo: The maid says no cats is the master's rule.
note.sakai.misshitsu/view:1: A shiromuku locked away deep inside, as if someone were shut in.
note.sakai.daidokoro/view:2: Someone keeps changing the flowers on the little grave.
note.sakai.daidokoro/act:grave: The little grave was made for a cat.
note.sakai.kyakuma/npc:yoshiyuki: The old master remembers the girl deep inside kept a cat.
note.sakai.omote/view:1: A grand house holding a wedding, and not one cat to be heard.
note.sakai.genkan/view:1: The old master sits in the reception room, saying nothing.
note.sakai.rouka/view:1: The servants avoid the door at the end of the red corridor.
note.sakai.kyakuma/view:1: The old master keeps looking at the crane on the screen.
note.sakai.ozashiki/view:1: The livelier the front, the quieter the back.
note.sakai.rouka/npc:odajima: The night watchman says the door at the back must not be opened.

act.sakai.grave.label: Press palms
act.sakai.grave.line: Incense smoke circles the grave once, like a cat brushing against your legs.

hold.sakai.理: What became of that girl? The answer is deep in the house.
pre.sakai.ozashiki: A bell rings once in the distance, then stops.

lines: Travelling this late? The rain hasn't eased one bit.
No children upstairs, but at night someone's always running.
I've gone up to look a few times. Not a soul.
In rain like this, only the room upstairs is still free.
The girls here in the old days couldn't keep a baby if they fell pregnant.
What this house used to be, guests had better not ask.
Thank you for letting me stay tonight.
I'm going to have this child, no matter what.
My family doesn't want it. I do.

act.wanya.listen.label: Listen
act.wanya.listen.line: A patter of small feet runs overhead. A shadow flickers at the end of the corridor.

act.wanya.jizo.label: Press palms
act.wanya.jizo.line: The red bibs are freshly changed. A pinwheel starts turning on its own.

hint.wanya.形: On the second-floor corridor, stop and listen.
hint.wanya.真: Something seems hidden behind the stones in the indoor garden.
hint.wanya.理: In the top-floor room, a guest is still awake.
hold.wanya.理: What do these children want? First you need to know what this house used to be.
pre.wanya.ozashiki: A child is laughing on the top floor. Come closer, and the laughing stops.

find.wanya.1.title: A tiny straw sandal
find.wanya.1.body: A straw sandal lies by the red bridge, no bigger than a palm, its cord freshly braided. The rain has soaked it through. The other one is nowhere to be found.

find.wanya.2.title: A small handprint on the fusuma
find.wanya.2.body: A handprint near the bottom of the fusuma paper, only knee-high. Short fingers, as if someone pressed there while pulling themselves up to stand.

find.wanya.3.title: A drum toy on the desk
find.wanya.3.body: A little pellet drum sits on the corner of the front desk, half its red lacquer worn away. Ask around, and no one can say which guest left it.

case.wanya.title: A rainy night at the Yorozuya
case.wanya.hook: A woman seeking shelter from the rain takes the top-floor room, and a mononoke follows. Without Form, Truth and Reason, the sword stays sheathed.

note.wanya.rouka/act:listen: On the second-floor corridor, small feet ran overhead.
note.wanya.genkan/npc:tokuji: The clerk says there are no children upstairs, yet someone runs at night.
note.wanya.niwa/view:2: Small figures are hidden behind the garden stones.
note.wanya.niwa/act:jizo: The little jizō wear new bibs. They are for children never born.
note.wanya.genkan/npc:hisayo: The proprietress says the girls here couldn't keep their babies.
note.wanya.ozashiki/view:1: The top-floor room is never given to guests.
note.wanya.ozashiki/npc:shino: Shino says she will have this child, no matter what.
note.wanya.soto/view:1: On the rainy night, only the top-floor windows are dark.
note.wanya.soto/view:2: The shadows by the bridge all look up at the floors above.
note.wanya.soto/view:3: The front is too grand for an ordinary inn.
note.wanya.genkan/view:1: Only the top-floor room was left.
note.wanya.rouka/view:1: The guests are asleep, but there are footsteps on the boards.
note.wanya.rouka/view:2: The farther down the corridor, the quieter.
note.wanya.niwa/view:1: A very quiet garden hidden inside the house.

lines: The new girls cry at night. I can't sleep.
That umbrella in the corridor opened by itself. No one touched it.
Whoever I tell, they all say to hold my tongue.
I only came this month. I haven't learned all the rules yet.
The little mirror I brought, does that have to go in the well too?
My mother gave it to me. I can't bear to.
Once you enter the Ōoku, you forget everything outside.
What's thrown away is gone. No one is to fish it out.
I have kept this rule myself for decades.

act.ooku.kasa.label: Look
act.ooku.kasa.line: The umbrella snaps half open on its own, then slowly folds shut.

act.ooku.well.label: Look in the well
act.ooku.well.line: A comb, a letter, a small doll float up in the water, then scatter.

act.ooku.closet.label: Open the closet
act.ooku.closet.line: A row of things in the closet, dripping wet, as if just back from the well.

hint.ooku.形: That old umbrella by the main corridor wall. Take a closer look.
hint.ooku.真: The well in the courtyard. Have you looked in?
hint.ooku.理: In Oyuki's empty room, the closet has stayed shut.
hold.ooku.理: Why do these things come back? The rule of the well isn't clear yet.
ready.ooku: Over in the main corridor, the umbrella makes a sound.

find.ooku.1.title: A dropped hairpin
find.ooku.1.body: A hairpin on the floor of the main corridor, one red bead missing from its head. Something so easy to see, and everyone passing acts as if it isn't there.

find.ooku.2.title: A paper crane under the window
find.ooku.2.body: A paper crane tucked under the round window, its folds still crisp. Something was written on one wing, but water has blurred it past reading.

find.ooku.3.title: An unfinished letter
find.ooku.3.body: A letter lies open on the writing desk. It begins "Dear Mother" and stops after one line. The ink is long dry; the brush still rests by the inkstone.

case.ooku.title: The well of the Ōoku
case.ooku.hook: In the corridors of the Ōoku, an umbrella opens with no one touching it. Without Form, Truth and Reason, the sword stays sheathed.

note.ooku.corridor/act:kasa: The old umbrella by the corridor wall opens on its own.
note.ooku.maids/npc:kame: Okame says the umbrella in the corridor opened by itself.
note.ooku.courtyard/view:1: New ladies-in-waiting must throw their treasures into the well.
note.ooku.courtyard/act:well: Shadows of a comb, a letter and a doll float at the bottom of the well.
note.ooku.maids/npc:asa: Oasa can't bear to throw away the mirror her mother gave her.
note.ooku.yuki/view:1: So many people in the Ōoku, yet one room has stood empty a long time.
note.ooku.yuki/act:closet: In the empty room's closet, a row of dripping-wet things.
note.ooku.utayama/npc:utayama: Utayama says no one may fish out what's been thrown away.
note.ooku.corridor/view:1: An old umbrella no one uses is tucked by the wall.
note.ooku.corridor/view:2: The beauties on the wall are all smiling.
note.ooku.maids/view:1: The things the new girls brought have all gone.
note.ooku.utayama/view:1: Utayama, who keeps the rules, has a very quiet room.

loc.fuenokouji.title: The Fuenokōji house
loc.fuenokouji.body: A noble residence in Kyoto, head house of the Fuenokōji school of incense. The snow keeps falling. Tonight an incense contest will choose the lady a husband. Episodes 8 and 9 of the TV series, "Nue", take place here, almost entirely in ink.

fuenokouji_mon.1.title: The gate in the snow
fuenokouji_mon.1.body: Snow lies deep before the gate. White walls edged in ink flank the board-roofed gate. Several guests came tonight, yet there isn't one footprint in the snow.

fuenokouji_mon.2.title: Earthen wall in the snow
fuenokouji_mon.2.body: Seen at an angle, an earthen wall runs off across the snow, bare trees beyond it. The whole house is only ink and white. Not a voice to be heard.

fuenokouji_niwa.1.title: The raised veranda
fuenokouji_niwa.1.body: A veranda raised in mid-air, railed all around, its steps wide and steep: a house in the shinden style. Tonight an incense contest inside will choose a husband. What does the winner get?

fuenokouji_niwa.2.title: Stone lantern in the snow garden
fuenokouji_niwa.2.body: Below the outer veranda lies the snow garden. Beside a stone lantern, a few rocks sit half buried, their moss still green. The snow should be untouched. Who left that line of small footprints?

fuenokouji_rouka.1.title: Lattice windows and shoji
fuenokouji_rouka.1.body: Lattice windows on one side of the corridor, a row of shoji on the other, the floorboards running far inside. You've walked a long time, and the snowlight outside hasn't changed. Why does dawn never come?

fuenokouji_rouka.2.title: Looking back down the corridor
fuenokouji_rouka.2.body: Looking back, the lattice and shoji on both sides are exactly alike. The door you came in by is already hard to make out.

fuenokouji_kou.1.title: The lady behind the blind
fuenokouji_kou.1.body: The Incense Room's dais is hung with a bamboo blind. Lady Ruri sits behind it, only her hem showing; no one has seen her face. Incense trays for the contest wait before it. Do the suitors all see the same woman?

fuenokouji_kou.2.title: The Tiger Room
fuenokouji_kou.2.body: A tiger is painted on the fusuma here. Someone recognises it as a copy of Nagasawa Rosetsu's Tiger. In the old tales, the Nue has a tiger's feet. Looking out from here, the snow hasn't stopped.

fuenokouji_oku.1.title: The Ink-Cloud Room
fuenokouji_oku.1.body: A high ceiling, ink clouds rolling across the fusuma, door pulls in the Genji-kō pattern. Farther in, a vermilion door comes into view. The deeper you go, the heavier the incense.

fuenokouji_oku.2.title: The Ink-Splash Room
fuenokouji_oku.2.body: Look up: walls and ceiling are spattered with ink, running down in streaks, as if someone fell here. Four suitors came to ask for her hand. Why did only three arrive?

fuenokouji_oku.3.title: The Red Room
fuenokouji_oku.3.body: The whole room is painted vermilion, the only colour in this house of ink. At the far end is a raised seat, empty. This is where the lady sits. Where is she now?

mononoke.fuenokouji.name: Nue
mononoke.fuenokouji.katachi: Everyone sees it differently. It is a Nue.
mononoke.fuenokouji.makoto: For the incense wood called Tōdai-ji, the people of this house died one by one.
mononoke.fuenokouji.kotowari: Everyone wanted it, so it became whatever each of them wanted.
mononoke.fuenokouji.itemBody: Wrapped in many layers of brocade, a length of blackened wood. Once lit, it fills the whole room with scent.
mononoke.fuenokouji.after: The scent drifts away, and the snow stops. Outside, it has long been spring.

lines: So many rules just to smell some incense. It's stifling.
Just now there was a little girl in the corridor. She turned around, and she was an old nun.
This house is cursed. Once I have the Tōdai-ji, I'm leaving.
This snow has fallen all night. Why won't it stop?
What becomes of the lady is no concern of mine. I want only the Tōdai-ji.
Smell that wood once and you never forget it.
Please, sit. The incense will be lit shortly.
The lady you each speak of, why is she different for everyone?
My eyes are poor. I don't know whom to believe.
An incense contest on a snowy night. How refined, how refined.
Thirty years I've been smelling incense. I can read this burner too.
The Tōdai-ji? Naturally, it will be mine.

act.fuenokouji.footprints.label: Study the tracks
act.fuenokouji.footprints.line: The small footprints turn into animal claws as they go, and end at the veranda.

act.fuenokouji.koubako.label: Open the chest
act.fuenokouji.koubako.line: Wrapped in many layers of brocade, a length of blackened, rotting wood.

hint.fuenokouji.形: Those footprints in the snow garden. Something's off.
hint.fuenokouji.真: The rooms deep in the house. No one dares go in.
hint.fuenokouji.理: The incense chest in the Incense Room holds the Tōdai-ji.
hold.fuenokouji.理: Why must they have it? What happened in this house isn't clear yet.

find.fuenokouji.1.title: A geta in the snow
find.fuenokouji.1.body: A single geta in the snow by the gate, its thong snapped. The snow around it is smooth. Not one footprint leads toward it.

find.fuenokouji.2.title: A sachet by the shoji
find.fuenokouji.2.body: A small sachet hangs by the shoji, embroidered with a Genji-kō pattern. In Genji-kō you smell five packets of incense. Each of the 52 possible answers is matched to a chapter of The Tale of Genji, and this pattern is one answer drawn out.

find.fuenokouji.3.title: A broken incense token
find.fuenokouji.3.body: A small broken slip of wood on the floor, a token for writing answers in the contest. On the back, where the name goes, it has been rubbed out.

case.fuenokouji.title: The Fuenokōji incense contest
case.fuenokouji.hook: An incense contest on a snowy night to choose a husband. Of four suitors, only three arrived. Without Form, Truth and Reason, the sword stays sheathed.

note.fuenokouji.niwa/act:footprints: The small footprints in the snow turn into animal claws.
note.fuenokouji.rouka/npc:muromachi: Muromachi says a little girl turned around and was an old nun.
note.fuenokouji.oku/view:2: The Ink-Splash Room looks as if someone fell there.
note.fuenokouji.oku/view:3: The raised seat in the Red Room is empty. The lady is gone.
note.fuenokouji.niwa/npc:nakarai: Nakarai says the lady is no concern of his. He wants only the Tōdai-ji.
note.fuenokouji.kou/view:1: Through the blind, no one has seen the lady's face.
note.fuenokouji.kou/act:koubako: The Tōdai-ji everyone fights over is a length of rotten wood.
note.fuenokouji.kou/npc:roni: The old nun says each of them describes a different lady.
note.fuenokouji.mon/view:1: Several guests came, but there are no footprints in the snow.
note.fuenokouji.mon/view:2: Not a voice anywhere in the house.
note.fuenokouji.niwa/view:1: Tonight an incense contest here will choose a husband.
note.fuenokouji.niwa/view:2: A line of small footprints in the snow garden.
note.fuenokouji.rouka/view:1: You've walked a long time, and dawn never comes.
note.fuenokouji.rouka/view:2: Looking back, the door you came in by is hard to see.
note.fuenokouji.kou/view:2: The tiger in the Tiger Room. They say the Nue has a tiger's feet.
note.fuenokouji.oku/view:1: The deeper in, the heavier the incense.

pre.fuenokouji.kou: Someone laughs softly behind the blind. The blind doesn't move.
end.sakai: The wedding never happened. There are fewer people in the house now, and the door to the innermost room stands open.
end.wanya: The rain has stopped, and the Yorozuya opens for guests as usual. Someone has gone up to tidy the top-floor room.
end.ooku: The next morning, the ladies-in-waiting comb their hair and go on duty as usual. The same footsteps in the corridor.
end.fuenokouji: No husband will be chosen by this contest. No one has lived in the house for a long time. Only a broken gate remains.

close.sakai.verdict: The wedding was for the guests. What this family feared most was anyone remembering what lay behind that door.
close.sakai.question: A door everyone walks around. Is this the only house that has one?

close.wanya.verdict: No one in this house was wicked. Only children, year after year, that no one kept, and those who didn't dare to.
close.wanya.question: To be wanted, truly, just once. What must that be like?

close.ooku.verdict: The rules were handed down, generation after generation. So were the things no one could bear to let go.
close.ooku.question: To stay, how much of themselves must people throw away before it is enough?

close.fuenokouji.verdict: For a piece of wood long since rotten, they lived the same night over and over.
close.fuenokouji.question: The thing wanted with everything one has. How many ever opened it?

mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.fuenokouji.name: White Bakeneko
mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.fuenokouji.katachi: White as the snow, only its eyes showing behind the blind: a White Bakeneko.
mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.fuenokouji.makoto: On the night of the incense contest, everyone wanted the place beside the lady.
mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.fuenokouji.kotowari: That place had always been its own. It would not be replaced.
mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.fuenokouji.itemBody: A few white hairs caught in the tassels of the blind. Lean close, and they still carry that night's incense.
mononoke.bakeneko_shiro.fuenokouji.after: The place behind the blind is empty now. There is nothing left to guard.

mononoke.noppera.fuenokouji.name: Noppera-bō
mononoke.noppera.fuenokouji.katachi: Lift the blind, and the face behind it is blank.
mononoke.noppera.fuenokouji.makoto: None of the suitors ever saw the lady's face. Each imagined one of his own.
mononoke.noppera.fuenokouji.kotowari: Given so many faces by others, she lost her own.
mononoke.noppera.fuenokouji.itemBody: A thin square of silk that fell from the blind. No one ever saw clearly the face behind it.
mononoke.noppera.fuenokouji.after: She gave back every face that others had given her.

out.fuenokouji: The incense has cleared. It looks brighter outside. Go and see.

intro.cards.t:
He is only a medicine seller.
Yet wherever he goes, strange things happen.
intro.cards.b: Ōoku · Yorozuya · Sakai house · Fuenokōji house

intro.cards.t:
Grudges, obsessions, things too dear to let go:
when they meet a spirit, they become a mononoke.

In the Medicine Seller's box there is a sword,
waiting for an answer.

What it is, what happened, why it will not leave.
Only with all three does the sword leave its sheath.

The rain is still falling.
But the story has already begun.

loc.solaris.title: The Solaris Maru
loc.solaris.body: A great ship of the Mikuniya, stacked tier on tier with pavilions in pink, blue-green and yellow, like a small town afloat on the sea. Episodes 3 to 5 of the TV series, "Umibōzu", take place here.

solaris_kanpan.1.title: The sea beyond the rail
solaris_kanpan.1.body: Beyond the pink rail lies the sea. Banners swell in the wind. The fog grows thicker. On the water stands a shadow, taller than the ship's towers. Is it a wave, or has something stood up?

solaris_kanpan.2.title: Looking back at the towers
solaris_kanpan.2.body: Looking back, the towers rise tier on tier, pink, blue-green, lemon yellow, like a small town afloat on the sea. In the middle of the deck lies a pool of duckweed.

solaris_nakaniwa.1.title: The whirlpool pond
solaris_nakaniwa.1.body: Tiers of galleries ring an open well. The pond at the bottom is painted with whirlpools, yet the water does not move at all. The yellow stairs are carpeted in large purple and green flowers.

solaris_nakaniwa.2.title: The fish ceiling panel
solaris_nakaniwa.2.body: Overhead, a hanabishi lattice ceiling. At its centre, a lemon-yellow coffered ceiling panel patterned with fish, a large red fish swimming in the middle. The people of this ship painted the sea above their heads.

solaris_rouka.1.title: The hanabishi corridor
solaris_rouka.1.body: The hanabishi lattice ceiling runs all the way in. Red and white lanterns hang on the pink wall to the left, cabin doors line the right, and at the end stands a white shoji.

solaris_rouka.2.title: The wall of charms
solaris_rouka.2.body: Row on row of paper charms cover the left wall, painted with eyes and whirlpools, one pasted over another. So many eyes. Where are they all looking?

solaris_kyaku.1.title: The phoenix painting
solaris_kyaku.1.body: A phoenix hangs on the main wall of the cabin, lattice windows on either side. The ship has entered the Dragon's Triangle, and the people here are still gambling.

solaris_kyaku.2.title: The cabin of red and white lanterns
solaris_kyaku.2.body: A pale blue-green floor, pink lattice framing it all around, a row of red and white lanterns overhead. The colours are so lively, yet the people sitting here hardly speak.

solaris_tomo.1.title: The red whirlpool sail
solaris_tomo.1.body: A single mast stands at the centre of the stern, flying a red sail painted with a whirlpool. Flowers cover the ship's side, and below them, a painted city on the sea floor.

solaris_tomo.2.title: The utsuro-bune on the sea
solaris_tomo.2.body: A small boat drifts on the sea to the northwest, nailed shut on all sides, no door, no window: an utsuro-bune, a sealed boat. Why does it keep following this ship?

mononoke.solaris.name: Umibōzu
mononoke.solaris.katachi: Rising from the sea in the fog: an Umibōzu.
mononoke.solaris.makoto: Oyō chose to take her brother's place in the sealed boat, and became the pillar that calms the sea.
mononoke.solaris.kotowari: What Genkei feared was never Oyō's hatred. It was his own heart.
mononoke.solaris.itemBody: A great iron nail, rusted through. Fifty years ago, this is what sealed the boards of the utsuro-bune.
mononoke.solaris.after: The fog lifts. He is young again, and seems to be smiling.

lines: I am Yanagi Gen'yōsai, a shugendō ascetic. For the spirits of this sea, ask me.
A shadow that large. No mistake, it is an Umibōzu.
No ship that enters the Dragon's Triangle has ever come out.
The master told us not to leave our cabins at night.
When the master was young, he had a sister. She took his place in the utsuro-bune.
The master never lets anyone speak of it.
For fifty years I have chanted sutras every day, for one person.
The sea became like this because of her.
She ought to hate me. Yet what I have feared all these years, it seems, was not her.
Medicine Seller? We meet again.
I was going to Edo to find a new house to serve. I never thought the voyage would go like this.
After what happened at the Sakai house, nothing frightens me. Probably.
That sword. Draw it and let me see.
There's no wind on this sea, yet the ship keeps moving.
Kanesada is stirring in its sheath. It wants to cut something.
Every day lost is a day's silver lost.
The compass? I checked it myself before we set out. It was fine.
The ship isn't moving anyway. A few more rounds.
Half my life at sea, and I've never seen water this still.
Someone has tampered with the compass. The needle keeps pointing the wrong way.
Until dawn, nobody goes up the mast.

act.solaris.biwa.label: Listen
act.solaris.biwa.line: The biwa asks what one fears most. A girl rises from the pond.

act.solaris.fuda.label: Study the charms
act.solaris.fuda.line: The eyes on the charms all face Genkei's cabin door.

act.solaris.utsuro.label: Examine the boat
act.solaris.utsuro.line: A crack has opened in the sealed boards. The utsuro-bune is empty.

hint.solaris.形: By the rail on the southwest side of the deck. Look out at the sea.
hint.solaris.真: Off the stern, a sealed boat drifts in the waves.
hint.solaris.理: By the whirlpool pond in the courtyard, something like the sound of a biwa.
hold.solaris.理: What does Genkei fear? Who once sat in the utsuro-bune isn't clear yet.
pre.solaris.kanpan: Off the bow, the sea swells once, then lies flat again.

find.solaris.1.title: Coins under the duckweed
find.solaris.1.body: A few coins caught among the duckweed, green with age. Someone must have made a wish here.

find.solaris.2.title: A pried compass lid
find.solaris.2.body: A brass compass lid, pry marks along its edge. Someone has tampered with the ship's compass.

find.solaris.3.title: A worn die
find.solaris.3.body: A die rolls out from under the gaming table, its corners worn round. With the ship stopped in the fog, who knows how many times it has been thrown.

case.solaris.title: The Solaris Maru adrift
case.solaris.hook: In the night, the ship strays into the Dragon's Triangle. In the fog, something rises from the sea. Without Form, Truth and Reason, the sword stays sheathed.

note.solaris.kanpan/view:1: On the foggy sea, a shadow taller than the ship's towers.
note.solaris.kanpan/npc:yanagi: Yanagi Gen'yōsai says the shadow is an Umibōzu.
note.solaris.tomo/act:utsuro: The utsuro-bune that drifted here is sealed tight, and empty inside.
note.solaris.rouka/npc:sogen: Sōgen says the master's sister took his place in the utsuro-bune.
note.solaris.nakaniwa/act:biwa: The biwa asked what one fears most; a girl rose from the pond.
note.solaris.rouka/act:fuda: The eyes on the charms all face Genkei's cabin door.
note.solaris.kyaku/npc:genkei: Genkei said that what he had feared all these years was perhaps not Oyō.
note.solaris.kanpan/view:2: The towers rise tier on tier, like a small town afloat.
note.solaris.nakaniwa/view:1: The water in the whirlpool pond does not move at all.
note.solaris.nakaniwa/view:2: A large red fish swims on the coffered ceiling panel.
note.solaris.rouka/view:1: At the end of the corridor, a white shoji.
note.solaris.rouka/view:2: The wall is covered in charms painted with eyes.
note.solaris.kyaku/view:1: The ship is in the Dragon's Triangle, and the cabin is still gambling.
note.solaris.kyaku/view:2: The cabin is bright with colour, yet the people hardly speak.
note.solaris.tomo/view:1: A red whirlpool sail flies at the stern.
note.solaris.tomo/view:2: An utsuro-bune with no door or window drifts on the sea.

end.solaris: The ship leaves the Dragon's Triangle. Somewhere on the sea, a voice softly says: brother.

close.solaris.verdict: What he feared was never the sea, nor his sister. It was the heart he could not rein in.
close.solaris.question: What people spend a lifetime running from: could it be only themselves?

loc.subway.title: The Subway
loc.subway.body: A subway line just opened in the last years of Taishō. The first train is full of people who drew first-ride tickets. The last three episodes of the TV series, "Bakeneko", take place here, every frame like an old, faded poster.

subway_homu.1.title: The platform under iron arches
subway_homu.1.body: White tiled walls above a band of green wainscot. Overhead, a barrel vault held up by iron ribs. A single car waits at the platform. At both ends, the tunnel mouths are too dark to see into.

subway_homu.2.title: The Fukuju Station sign
subway_homu.2.body: The sign reads Fukuju Station. Beside it, a row of new posters, all celebrating the subway's opening. Before this line opened, what happened here?

subway_sharyo.1.title: The first train's carriage
subway_sharyo.1.body: Long benches run along both walls. Overhead, two rows of brass hand straps and a row of milk-white globe lamps. Beyond the windows, only black. The train keeps moving. It doesn't stop once.

subway_sharyo.2.title: The painting by the door
subway_sharyo.2.body: By the carriage door hangs a painting of a beauty: a white-haired woman, a black cat in her arms. Everyone aboard says they have never seen it before. The cat in the painting. Who is it watching?

subway_kaisatsu.1.title: The wooden ticket gates
subway_kaisatsu.1.body: Two wooden ticket gates, a row of wooden railings, a clock hanging from the ceiling. The ticket collector clips a corner off each first-ride ticket and lets people through, one by one.

subway_kaisatsu.2.title: The poster wall
subway_kaisatsu.2.body: Posters cover the wall: films, cosmetics, the subway's opening. Everyone in them is smiling. Everyone walking past keeps their head down.

subway_kissa.1.title: The stained-glass windows
subway_kissa.1.body: A row of stained-glass windows, a half-moon of coloured glass above the door. The light falls on a black-and-white checkered floor. A café waitress carries coffee back and forth.

subway_kissa.2.title: The counter
subway_kissa.2.body: Rows of bottles behind the counter, a clock on the wall. One café waitress is always at the end of the counter, practising expressions in the mirror. She wants to be in films.

mononoke.subway.name: Bakeneko
mononoke.subway.katachi: The woman holding a cat, whom only the child can see. She is the Bakeneko.
mononoke.subway.makoto: Setsuko did not jump. She was pushed from the overpass.
mononoke.subway.kotowari: All she wanted was one true word, and no one on the train would say it.
mononoke.subway.itemBody: A charred corner of manuscript paper, only half a line left: "The Mayor... construction funds..." The article never made it into print.
mononoke.subway.after: The train stops. People walk out of the station. A bird has settled on the arched ceiling.

lines: The milk has to be delivered before dawn.
There's a lady in the carriage holding a cat. Only I can see her.
She keeps looking at the man in the flat cap.
This train... it won't stop. The brakes don't work.
That night, what I ran over was a cat. Wasn't it?
I wasn't asleep. I only closed my eyes for a moment.
My mother-in-law thinks I'm at home saying the nembutsu.
That night I was under the overpass. I heard people arguing up above.
If I tell that, I'll have to tell what I was doing there too.
Someday I'm going to be in films.
Setsuko came by the café. She said she'd put the truth in the paper.
When the police came asking, I said I didn't know her.
Moriya, of the Maiasa Daily. I'm on this train to write a story.
Setsuko? A shame. She was a good reporter.
An article? What article. She never turned one in.
Today is a fine day for this city.
This subway is my doing, start to finish. Rest assured, all of you.
Dirty money? Something the papers made up.

act.subway.senro.label: Check the rails
act.subway.senro.line: An old stain on a sleeper that won't wash out. Cat pawprints beside it.

act.subway.shinbun.label: Read the paper
act.subway.shinbun.line: A small item in the corner of an old paper: woman reporter leaps from bridge.

hint.subway.形: The cat in the painting by the carriage door. Its eyes are open.
hint.subway.真: On the rails beside the platform, an old stain remains.
hint.subway.理: The waitress at the café by the station seems to have met that reporter.
hold.subway.理: What did she want? How she died isn't clear yet.
pre.subway.homu: Deep in the tunnel, a cat cries once.

find.subway.1.title: An empty milk bottle
find.subway.1.body: An empty milk bottle, its paper cap still on. The milk boy dropped it. Not one bottle has been delivered today.

find.subway.2.title: A clipped first-ride ticket
find.subway.2.body: A first-ride souvenir ticket printed 'First Ride, Fukuju Station, Opening Day', its corner clipped.

find.subway.3.title: An actress's photograph
find.subway.3.body: A photograph of an actress, cut out, tucked under the sugar bowl. On the back is written: Someday.

case.subway.title: The first train from Fukuju Station
case.subway.hook: The first train pulls out and never stops. Everyone aboard is tied to a woman reporter who died. Without Form, Truth and Reason, the sword stays sheathed.

note.subway.sharyo/view:2: The painting of a beauty by the door, a black cat in her arms.
note.subway.homu/npc:masao: Masao says a lady holding a cat is in the carriage, and only he can see her.
note.subway.homu/act:senro: An old stain on the rails, a few cat pawprints beside it.
note.subway.homu/npc:kinoshita: The driver says what he ran over that night was a cat.
note.subway.kaisatsu/npc:haru: That night Haru was under the overpass, and heard people arguing above.
note.subway.kissa/npc:chiyo: Chiyo says Setsuko meant to put the truth in the paper.
note.subway.kissa/act:shinbun: In the corner of an old paper: woman reporter leaps from bridge.
note.subway.sharyo/npc:moriya: Moriya says Setsuko never turned in an article.
note.subway.homu/view:1: At both ends, the tunnel mouths are too dark to see into.
note.subway.homu/view:2: The posters all celebrate the opening. No one looks at the rails.
note.subway.sharyo/view:1: The train keeps moving. It doesn't stop once.
note.subway.kaisatsu/view:1: A corner clipped from each first-ride ticket, people pass in one by one.
note.subway.kaisatsu/view:2: The people on the posters smile. The people passing keep their heads down.
note.subway.kissa/view:1: The coloured light falls on the black-and-white checkered floor.
note.subway.kissa/view:2: A café waitress practises expressions in the mirror.

end.subway: Later, a few bunches of flowers appear on the overpass. The paper prints what the mayor did.

close.subway.verdict: Only one pair of hands pushed her. A whole train of people watched her die.
close.subway.question: The things people see and never say. How many do they gather in one lifetime?

loc.prison.title: The Prison
loc.prison.body: The cell where Ochō is held. Condemned for killing her husband's family, she waits to be beheaded. Episodes 6 and 7 of the TV series, "Noppera-bō", take place here, half in the prison, half in a dream of her own.

prison_ro.1.title: Ochō's cell
prison_ro.1.body: Behind the wooden bars lies a straw mat. Ochō kneels on it, her back perfectly straight. Sentenced to death, she has never once cried that she was wronged.

prison_ro.2.title: The cell to the north
prison_ro.2.body: In the cell to the north sits a medicine chest. A lock hangs on every cell door, and each looks secure. But are they really locked?

prison_zashiki.1.title: The mural
prison_zashiki.1.body: The whole west wall is a gold-ground mural of women in kimono, each one sitting properly. Not one of them is smiling.

prison_zashiki.2.title: The Sasaki zashiki
prison_zashiki.2.body: Dark wooden floor, a board ceiling, fusuma painted with plum branches and small birds. A pink cabinet in the corner, two boxes stacked. Ochō kneels in this room, waiting to be told what to do.

prison_daidokoro.1.title: Rack and black door
prison_daidokoro.1.body: White jars and pink bowls on the red-lacquered rack, a green bamboo basket beside it. Next to the rack, a black board door that seems to lead somewhere else.

prison_daidokoro.2.title: Stove and jars
prison_daidokoro.2.body: The fire in the stove went out long ago. A row of clay jars stands beside it; the oldest still has a label, the name scraped off. How many wives has this house had?

mononoke.prison.name: Noppera-bō
mononoke.prison.katachi: One who lost her own face for the sake of others' wishes: a Noppera-bō.
mononoke.prison.makoto: In that house, day by day, she killed her own self. The cell door was never locked.
mononoke.prison.kotowari: She tried to carry her mother's wishes, and carrying them, her heart grew crooked.
mononoke.prison.itemBody: A white fox mask. Turned over, a woman's face is painted on the back, with Ochō's eyes and brows.
mononoke.prison.after: The end of the long corridor opens. Coloured paper drifts down from the sky.

lines: Medicine Seller, please don't trouble yourself over me.
Mother said to bear it, and all would be well. I have always borne it.
Who did I kill? ... I don't remember.
Ochō, come with me. This cell door can't hold you.
I can wear any face. Whichever face Ochō wants, that is the face I'll be.
Marry me, Ochō. This time, all you need do is smile.
Marrying into the Sasaki house is the greatest fortune our family could ask for.
Next time it must be a boy. The Sasakis need an heir.
No crying. Would a mother ever harm her own daughter?
Supper still not ready? Dawdling again.
The last wife hanged herself, right here in this kitchen.
Whoever comes through this door keeps this house's rules.
Where's the tea?
Don't shame me in front of others.
I only married her as a favour to her mother.

act.prison.door.label: Push the door
act.prison.door.line: The cell door opens at a push. The lock was never fastened.

hint.prison.形: Look along the row of small Noh masks in the wedding room, one by one.
hint.prison.真: Something is off about the lock on Ochō's cell door.
hint.prison.理: The temari doors in the plum room look like something from someone's childhood.
hold.prison.理: Why does she endure it? The life she led in that house isn't clear yet.

find.prison.1.title: An unlit pipe
find.prison.1.body: A long, slender pipe, its bowl clean. It has never been lit. The man in the fox mask carries one just like it.

find.prison.2.title: A half-wound temari ball
find.prison.2.body: A temari ball, its coloured thread wound only halfway. Wound with great care, as if afraid of a scolding for a mistake.

find.prison.3.title: A wedding notice, name blotted out
find.prison.3.body: A wedding notice. The bride's name has been blotted out in ink. Only the groom's side remains.

case.prison.title: Ochō's cell
case.prison.hook: Condemned for killing the Sasakis, Ochō sits in her cell awaiting death. A man in a fox mask comes to take her out and marry her. Without Form, Truth and Reason, the sword stays sheathed.

note.prison.ro/act:door: The lock on Ochō's cell door was never fastened.
note.prison.daidokoro/npc:shuto: Her mother-in-law says the last wife hanged herself in the kitchen.
note.prison.daidokoro/view:2: On the oldest jar, the name has been scraped off.
note.prison.ro/npc:ocho: Ochō says her mother told her to endure, and she always has.
note.prison.zashiki/view:1: Not one woman in the mural is smiling.
note.prison.ro/view:1: Sentenced to death, Ochō has never once said she was wronged.
note.prison.ro/view:2: A medicine chest sits in the cell to the north.
note.prison.zashiki/view:2: Ochō kneels in the zashiki, waiting for orders.
note.prison.daidokoro/view:1: A black door by the rack, leading somewhere else.
note.prison.ume/npc:kitsune: The man in the fox mask says whatever face Ochō wants, he will be.
note.prison.konrei/npc:haha: Her mother only frets: next time it must be a boy.
note.prison.konrei/view:2: A row of small Noh masks on the wall; one face after another.
note.prison.ume/view:2: Temari painted on the doors, like childhood toys.
note.prison.konrei/view:1: At this wedding, Ochō is smiling.
note.prison.owari/view:1: At the end of the corridor, gold and purple clouds.
note.prison.owari/view:2: Sky overhead; the paper vanishes as it falls.
note.prison.yume/view:1: No walls in the plum grove, only blossoms.
note.prison.yume/view:2: A door among the blossoms, like the kitchen's.

end.prison: The cell door stands open. No one is inside.

close.prison.verdict: She killed no one. Each time she answered "yes", a little less of her remained.
close.prison.question: To please others, how many times will a person put away their own face?

prison_konrei.1.title: Screen of Fuji and cranes
prison_konrei.1.body: A screen striped red and white, painted with Mount Fuji and cranes. Before it, two red cushions: the couple's seats. At this wedding, Ochō is smiling.

prison_konrei.2.title: Small Noh masks
prison_konrei.2.body: Gold walls with a great tree and deer, and a row of small Noh masks: white, purple, red, blue. One mask after another. Where is the face?

prison_ume.1.title: The elephant incense box
prison_ume.1.body: Red and white plum blossoms cover the walls, with a row of pink lattice doors. In the middle lies a sky-blue incense box shaped like an elephant, its trunk curled upward, open at the back, big enough to sit in.

prison_ume.2.title: The temari doors
prison_ume.2.body: White sliding doors painted with temari balls of every size, like childhood toys. As a child, did Ochō ever once play for herself?

prison_owari.1.title: The end of the corridor
prison_owari.1.body: Grey wooden corridors run on and on. At the far end the whole wall is sky: gold and purple clouds, a pine, a small temple.

prison_owari.2.title: Falling paper
prison_owari.2.body: Halfway down the corridor, there is sky overhead too. Coloured paper drifts down piece by piece and vanishes as it lands.

pre.prison.konrei: Behind the screen, someone laughs softly.

prison_yume.1.title: Painted plum grove
prison_yume.1.body: No walls. Ground and sky are broad strokes of pastel. Dark red-brown plum trees twist, streaked with blue, red blossoms on their branches.

prison_yume.2.title: A door on its own
prison_yume.2.body: Looking back, a black board door stands alone among the blossoms, just like the one in the kitchen. The kitchen can no longer be seen from here.

prelude.ooku.title: The depths of Edo Castle
prelude.ooku.body: At the innermost part of Edo Castle lies the Ōoku, the shogun's inner palace. Several hundred women live here, and no man but the shogun may enter. Rule is pressed upon rule. The corridors are always quiet.

prelude.ooku.title: The well in the courtyard
prelude.ooku.body: A maid newly come to the Ōoku must throw a treasured thing from home into the courtyard well, and so cut her ties with the world outside. Of late, an old umbrella lies in the main corridor. No one touches it. It opens on its own.

prelude.ooku.title: The door no man passes
prelude.ooku.body: The Medicine Seller, his chest on his back, passes through the door no man may pass. Why the umbrella opens, what lies at the bottom of the well, the maids dare not say. The paintings on the walls and the old things in the rooms are more honest than people.

prelude.wanya.title: Rain at the Yorozuya
prelude.wanya.body: An old inn, floor stacked on floor, its front far grander than any ordinary inn's. Years ago, it was a brothel. Tonight the rain has not let up.

prelude.wanya.title: The top-floor room
prelude.wanya.body: The largest zashiki on the top floor is never given to guests. Tonight a woman with child comes through the rain seeking a room, and it is the only one left. Overhead, on the floorboards, small footsteps begin.

prelude.wanya.title: One night, one roof
prelude.wanya.body: The Medicine Seller also takes a room at the Yorozuya tonight. No child is staying upstairs, yet something runs there. Neither the clerk nor the proprietress can say why. The furnishings, the small things in the corners, wait for someone to look closely.

prelude.sakai.title: The Sakai wedding
prelude.sakai.body: A respectable samurai household. Today its daughter marries. A great curtain bearing the family crest on red hangs at the gate. Guests arrive wave after wave, and the whole house is busy from top to bottom.

prelude.sakai.title: A house without cats
prelude.sakai.body: So large a house, and not one cat's cry. When mice get into the kitchen, there are only traps. Deep inside the house is a door, and the servants carrying things go the long way around it.

prelude.sakai.title: A medicine seller calls
prelude.sakai.body: On the wedding day, a medicine seller with a chest on his back comes to the door, and is in no hurry to leave. Kitchen, corridor, guest room: whatever this family hides will have left some trace.

prelude.fuenokouji.title: A noble house in snow
prelude.fuenokouji.body: A noble residence in Kyoto, head house of the Fuenokōji school of incense. The snow keeps falling. Nothing is left of the house but ink and white.

prelude.fuenokouji.title: Incense to choose a husband
prelude.fuenokouji.body: Tonight an incense contest will choose the lady a husband. The winner will also receive a piece of incense wood called Tōdai-ji. Of four suitors, only three have come.

prelude.fuenokouji.title: No footprints in the snow
prelude.fuenokouji.body: There is not one footprint in the snow, yet the Medicine Seller already stands at the gate. This night seems never to reach dawn. Everyone in the house has something on their mind, and what is said aloud is not always true.

prelude.solaris.title: Pavilions on the sea
prelude.solaris.body: The Solaris Maru, a great ship of the Mikuniya, built up tier on tier with pavilions in pink, blue-green and yellow, like a small town afloat on the sea. This voyage is bound for Edo.

prelude.solaris.title: The Dragon's Triangle
prelude.solaris.body: In the night someone tampered with the compass, and the ship strayed into the Dragon's Triangle. No ship that enters has ever come out. The fog grows thicker. Something is moving on the water.

prelude.solaris.title: Those aboard
prelude.solaris.body: Aboard are a high priest and his disciple, a shugendō ascetic, a samurai with his sword, and Kayo, a maid who left the Sakai house. The Medicine Seller is aboard too. Whatever lies in the fog must be asked of these people.

prelude.subway.title: The Taishō subway
prelude.subway.body: In the last years of Taishō, the city's first subway line opens. The platform at Fukuju Station is packed. Passengers who drew first-ride tickets board the first train.

prelude.subway.title: The first train never stops
prelude.subway.body: Once it pulls out, it never stops again. Beyond the windows, only black. A few months ago, a woman reporter fell from the overpass. The papers said she jumped.

prelude.subway.title: The same carriage
prelude.subway.body: The mayor, a detective, a newspaperman, a café waitress, a milk boy. The Medicine Seller is in this carriage too. Between these people seems to run a thread no one can see.

prelude.prison.title: Ochō's cell
prelude.prison.body: In the dark green cell, Ochō kneels on a straw mat, her back perfectly straight. She married into the Sasaki house. Now, condemned for killing her husband's family, she waits to be beheaded.

prelude.prison.title: The man in the fox mask
prelude.prison.body: Sentenced to death, she has not once cried that she was wronged. In the night, a man in a fox mask comes to the cell and says he will take her out of here and marry her.

prelude.prison.title: The cell next door
prelude.prison.body: The Medicine Seller is held in the cell to the north. To understand Ochō, one must walk into the house she remembers, and into the dream she dreams.
